title: AER-1 ACP interop fixture — observation rows joined by name
description: Machine-readable observation rows for the pinned AER-1 corpus. Any implementation can run the same set, publish its own observer column joined on vector name, and state its compared scope honestly. The fixture carries its scope on its face; it does not claim conformance, certification, or that any described work happened.

profile.text: AER-1 observation profile (ACP interop). An observer runs the pinned AER-1 corpus and publishes its own column over the same rows, joined on vector name, against the kit release and evaluated-set digest stated in the fixture manifest. Every claimed row carries the observer's stable name, what it read, and one of the five run-level outcomes: verified, verification_failed, not_checked, absent, unresolvable_record. not_checked carries exactly one of the six frozen reasons: access_refused, unsupported_family, schema_not_implemented, outside_scope, provenance_not_present, not_yet_materialized. A column claims per-vector comparison only where a per-vector verdict is actually measured; family-level-only lines stay explicitly unclaimed, and the compared scope is printed on the fixture's face. Two rules are load-bearing: no invented timestamps on corpus reads, and no execution language for fixture reads. verified means the check the observer recomputed matched the claim it evaluated; it is not proof the described work happened, and it is not a conformance claim or a certification. When a per-vector kit emit lands for the remaining families, columns widen on evidence, and the divergence count stays honest wherever it lands.
